points.description: Pseudocode initialises the weights (e.g. randomly or to zero) and goes through the labelled (+/-) training examples, updating the weights only for misclassified examples using w ← w + η·x (or the equivalent signed form w ← w + η·y·x for label y). Equivalent notation or a correct alternative update form earns the mark.

The pseudocode repeats the pass over all training examples (epochs) until the weights stop changing (or change very little), i.e. it iterates to convergence. Equivalent stopping criteria, such as 'until no examples are misclassified', earn the mark.

deductions.description: Update rule is wrong, for example adding x for correctly classified points or using a condition that does not detect misclassification.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for a pseudocode learning loop that initialises the weights, updates on misclassified examples with the perceptron rule, and repeats over epochs until the weights stop changing. One mark for each of the two points; the 'converges because data is linearly separable' remark in the model answer is a side comment and is not required. Give no marks for a description that does not give an algorithm or uses no weight update.
